sources.entry: kettanaito/naming-cheatsheet: : comprehensive language-agnostic guidelines on variables naming. Home of the A/HC/LC pattern.

summary.one_liner: A language-agnostic naming guide for variables and functions, with JavaScript examples, that introduces the A/HC/LC (prefix, action, high context, low context) pattern for function names.
summary.what_it_does: This is a written cheatsheet rather than a software project. It covers general naming rules: use English, pick one naming convention and stay consistent, keep names short, intuitive and descriptive, avoid contractions, and avoid repeating the surrounding context in a name. It proposes a pattern for function names (prefix? + action + high context + low context?) with a table of examples. It then lists common action verbs (get, set, reset, remove, delete, compose, handle) and prefixes (is, has, should, min/max, prev/next), explaining when each fits. It also gives guidance on singular versus plural names for variables holding one value or many.
use_cases: Choosing names for variables and functions in a codebase
Deciding between remove and delete for a function name
Writing boolean names such as isX, hasX, or shouldX
Reviewing code for naming consistency during code review
Teaching naming conventions to new developers
Naming callback handlers and getter functions
notable: Proposes the A/HC/LC pattern for function naming, with a worked table of examples
Explains the difference between remove and delete, and between add and create
Shows that word order changes meaning, e.g. shouldUpdateComponent versus shouldComponentUpdate
Covers a practical set of action verbs and prefixes with short code examples
caveats: Examples are JavaScript only, though the principles are stated to apply to any language
Guidance is opinionated and presented as suggestions rather than enforced rules
The README references an external article for the add/create discussion but does not include it
